topic.title: Foundations
topic.shortdesc: The building blocks: DITA as a source format, EPUB as a delivery format, and the transformation that connects them.

body.p: Before diving into configuration and advanced features, it is worth understanding the two standards that the DITA2ePub plugin bridges: DITAdefinitionDITA on the authoring side and EPUBdefinitionEPUB on the delivery side. This chapter introduces both, explains why the combination is powerful, and gives you a mental model for how the transformation works.

section.title: What Is DITA?
section.p: DITA — the Darwin Information Typing ArchitectureDarwin Information Typing Architecture — is an XML-based standard for creating, managing, and publishing content. Originally developed at IBM in the early 2000s and later standardized by OASISOASIS, DITA has become the dominant structured authoring framework for enterprise technical documentationAs of 2024, DITA is used by over 80% of Fortune 500 companies that produce structured technical documentation, according to industry surveys by The Content Wrangler..

ul.li: topic-based authoringTopic-based authoring — content is organized into self-contained topics, each covering a single subject. Topics can be assembled into publications using maps.
structured authoringStrong typing — DITA defines specialized topic types (concept, task, reference, glossary entry) with constrained content models, ensuring consistency across authors and teams.
Reuse — content can be shared across publications through conrefconref (content reference), keyrefkeyref (key-based reference), and conditional processing attributes.
multi-channel publishingMulti-channel output — a single set of source files can be transformed into PDF, HTML, EPUB, and other formats through the DITA Open Toolkit's plugin architecture.

section.title: What Is EPUB 3?
section.p: EPUBspecificationEPUB 3 is the current version of the Electronic Publication standard, maintained by the W3CW3C since 2017. It defines a container format for reflowable digital documents built on web technologies: XHTML 5 for content, CSS 3 for styling, and SVG for vector graphics.

An EPUB file is, at its core, a ZIP archive with a specific structureThe ZIP format was chosen for its universal support and compression capabilities. The mimetype file must appear first in the archive and must not be compressed, to allow reading systems to identify the file type without fully decompressing it.:

Points to the OPF package document. May also include encryption.xml for obfuscated fonts.
The package document: Dublin Core metadata, a manifest listing every file in the EPUB, and a spine defining the reading order.
The navigation document: table of contents, landmarks, and optionally a page list.
